answer: A farm that parks keys in the jury pool thus watches its influence decay while paying the wander fee to keep them eligible. Because the mirror decay is applied at each close, the atlas audit publishes the reduced weight and the seat has to be earned again. A juror that skips cases loses 9% of its weight per missed epoch, so sitting on a seat without doing the work is not a passive strategy. A 119 account operation therefore ties up 33 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
